subject: AWS Marketplace product page — copy + entitlements checklist
messages:
From: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0000
Subject: Marketplace listing help: timing + entitlements

Hi Marcus,

We're aiming to get the Acme Analytics integration listed on AWS Marketplace by the week of March 22. AWS asked us to confirm: product page copy, entitlements (per-seat vs. usage metering), pricing SKU structure, and who will be the Marketplace contact for co-sell registration.

Attached is a short PDF of the AWS requirements and our current internal positioning. Can Redwood help review the product page copy and recommend the best approach for SaaS metering vs private offers?

Key constraints: minimal changes to procurement flows for our customers, and we need to surface SOC2 and VPC options clearly on the listing.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 30m call if helpful.

Best,
Sarah
Head of Partnerships, Acme Analytics

Attachment: acme_listing_requirements.pdf

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 11:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing help: timing + entitlements

Thanks Sarah — looping in Grace (partnerships / co-sell) and Laura (sales ops) so we can align on listing model and go-to-market. Quick notes after a first pass: 

- We'll take the product page copy and reshape the top section for Marketplace (short 1-line summary, 3 bullet value props, short security paragraph).
- For entitlements: recommend SaaS metering (usage-based) if you expect variable volume; otherwise a seat-based SKU with optional metered overage. Grace, thoughts on co-sell implications?
- I attached an initial draft of the product page and our current pricing workbook — please review and drop comments.

Next steps:
- Grace: confirm co-sell eligibility and any AMI vs SaaS constraints with AWS contacts by EOD 3/3.
- Laura: prepare a private-offer pricing template and DocuSign flow for Acme.
- Sarah: confirm the primary contact for Marketplace operations and procurement on your side.

I'll schedule a 30m sync for Wednesday if that works.

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments: marketplace_product_page_draft.md; pricing_sheet_v3.xlsx

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 02 Mar 2026 13:40:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing help: timing + entitlements

Agree with Marcus' suggestions. A few additional operational items from the co-sell perspective: 

- Co-sell: we should register the opportunity in AWS PRM before listing to ensure eligibility for joint engagements. Tom (AWS) often requires the seller central contact and a partner rep.
- Entitlements: if Acme prefers predictable billing for enterprise buyers, offer a seat SKU plus optional usage metering SKU for overages — that gives customers procurement flexibility and keeps co-sell economics simple.
- Private Offers: prepare a private offer template; AWS will need a contact and a marketplace listing contact email (we should use marketplace@redwood.com).

Compliance note: include a short "Security & Data" section on the product page: SOC 2 Type II, optional VPC peering, and KMS support. AWS reviewers like that up front.

I'll check with our AWS partner manager this afternoon and confirm any additional metadata required (metering dimensions, SKU ids).

Grace
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@acmeanalytics.com>
Date: Tue, 03 Mar 2026 08:22:00 -0000
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing help: timing + entitlements

Nice summary — tagging a few copy edits and checklist items. Inline suggestions: 

1) Headline: shorten to "Redwood Inference for Acme Analytics — Low-latency LLM inference for analytics apps"
2) One-liner: "Deploy LLM inference in minutes with predictable latency and cost controls—hosted, dedicated, or private."
3) 3 bulleted value props (concise):
   - "Predictable per-token economics with intelligent batching & caching"
   - "Deployment modes: Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, Private VPC/on-prem"
   - "Enterprise-grade security: SOC 2, KMS, VPC peering"
4) Features section: include "SaaS metering option (usage-based), seat licensing, private offers / negotiated pricing"
5) Pricing callout: "Contact us for Private Offers and custom enterprise pricing" — link to DocuSign for the purchase agreement.

Logistics: AWS requires a marketplace contact and a 24/7 support contact on file; Marcus, can you provide the marketplace@redwood.com mailbox and a support rotation? Also attach the AWS checklist (I pulled their checklist PDF).

I added small copy edits to the draft and re-uploaded as v2. Also flagged the "marketing blurb" for the top of the page — avoid technical jargon there.

Laura
Director, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

Attachment: aws_listing_checklist.pdf
